en: Hello, who is speaking, please?
context: When you answer an unknown number.
explain: We use "is speaking" for who is on the phone. "Please" makes it polite.

en: I will call you back in ten minutes.
tamil: நான் பத்து நிமிஷத்துல உங்களுக்கு திருப்பி கூப்பிடறேன்.
context: When you are busy and cannot talk now.
explain: "Will" shows a promise. "Call back" means to phone again later.

alt.en: I'll ring you back after the meeting.
alt.tamil: மீட்டிங் முடிஞ்சதும் நான் உங்களுக்கு திருப்பி கூப்பிடறேன்.

en: Sorry, I missed your call earlier.
tamil: மன்னிச்சுக்கோங்க, முன்னாடி உங்க கால எடுக்க முடியல.
context: When you see a missed call and ring back.
explain: "Missed" is the past of "miss". We say "miss a call" when we do not answer.

alt.en: Sorry, I could not pick up your call.

en: I can't hear you properly.
context: When the line is bad.
explain: "Can't hear" is a very common phrase for a poor line.

en: The network is very weak here.
context: When the signal is poor in a place.
explain: Use "is" with "network". "Weak" describes a poor signal.

en: Can you hear me now?
context: After you move to a better signal.
explain: Start with "can" to ask if something is possible. "Now" shows you just tried something.

en: Please leave a message after the beep.
tamil: பீப் சத்தத்துக்கு அப்புறம் ஒரு மெசேஜ் விடுங்க.
context: A voicemail greeting.
explain: We use the base verb for a command. "Please" makes it a polite request.

en: Could you please ask him to call me back?
context: When the person you want is not available.
explain: "Could you" is a polite way to ask. "Ask him to call" means give him a message.

alt.en: Can you tell him to ring me?

en: He is on another call right now.
context: When you answer for a busy colleague.
explain: "Is on a call" means he is busy talking to someone.

en: Hold on, I will transfer your call.
tamil: கொஞ்சம் இருங்க, உங்க காலை மாத்தி விடறேன்.
context: When you connect a caller to someone else.
explain: "Hold on" means wait. "Transfer" means to send the call to another person.

en: I have been trying to reach you since morning.
tamil: நான் காலையில இருந்து உங்கள தொடர்பு கொள்ள முயற்சி பண்றேன்.
context: When you called many times without luck.
explain: "Have been trying" shows something that started in the past and continues. "Since" gives the starting time.

alt.en: I have been calling you all morning.
alt.tamil: நான் காலை முழுக்க உங்களுக்கு கூப்பிட்டுட்டே இருக்கேன்.

en: Your phone was switched off yesterday.
tamil: உங்க போன் நேத்து ஸ்விட்ச் ஆஃப்ல இருந்துச்சு.
context: When you could not reach someone.
explain: "Was" is used with "phone" in the past. "Switched off" means the phone was not on.

en: Did you get my voicemail?
context: When you left a voice message earlier.
explain: Use "did" with the base verb "get" to ask about the past.

en: I am calling about my internet bill.
context: When you start a customer care call.
explain: "I am calling about" is a polite way to say why you phoned.

en: My internet has not been working since yesterday.
tamil: என் இன்டர்நெட் நேத்துல இருந்து வேலை செய்யல.
context: When you complain to customer care.
explain: "Has not been working" shows a problem that began in the past and is still there.

alt.en: My internet is not working at all.

en: Can I speak to someone in Tamil, please?
context: When you want help in your own language.
explain: "Can I speak to" is the usual way to ask for a person on the phone.

en: Could you give me your complaint number?
context: What a customer care agent may ask.
explain: "Could you" is a polite request. "Complaint number" is the reference number.

en: Your call is important to us.
context: A common customer care message.
explain: This is a fixed phrase used by call centres. "Important to us" means we value it.

en: Please stay on the line.
context: When an agent makes you wait.
explain: "Stay on the line" means do not hang up. We use the base verb for polite orders.

en: I have been on hold for twenty minutes.
context: When customer care keeps you waiting.
explain: "Have been" plus a time period shows how long something has continued.

alt.en: I have been waiting for half an hour.
alt.tamil: நான் அரை மணி நேரமா காத்துட்டு இருக்கேன்.

en: Can you share your screen, please?
context: In a video call when someone needs to see your work.
explain: "Share your screen" is the common phrase in online meetings.

en: Your video is not working.
context: In a video call when the camera is off.
explain: "Is not working" tells us something is not functioning right now.

en: Please turn on your camera.
tamil: தயவு செய்து உங்க கேமராவை ஆன் பண்ணுங்க.
context: In an online class or meeting.
explain: "Turn on" is a phrasal verb. Use the base form for a request.

alt.en: Could you switch on your camera?

en: You are on mute.
context: When someone talks but we cannot hear them.
explain: "On mute" means the microphone is off.

en: Let me unmute myself.
context: When you start speaking in an online meeting.
explain: "Let me" plus a base verb is a polite way to say you will do something.

en: The call got cut suddenly.
context: When the call drops in the middle.
explain: "Got cut" is a spoken way to say the call ended by itself.

en: Sorry, you are breaking up.
tamil: மன்னிச்சுக்கோங்க, உங்க குரல் கட் கட்டா கேக்குது.
context: When the voice goes on and off.
explain: "Breaking up" means the sound keeps stopping because of a weak signal.

en: I'll send you a message on WhatsApp.
context: When talking is hard and texting is easier.
explain: "I'll" is a short form of "I will". We use it for quick decisions.

en: Will you be free this evening?
context: When you plan to call someone later.
explain: "Will you be" asks about a future situation.

en: Don't call me during the meeting.
context: When you tell someone not to disturb you.
explain: "Don't" plus a base verb is a negative command.

en: I never pick up unknown numbers.
tamil: தெரியாத நம்பர் கால நான் எப்பவும் எடுக்க மாட்டேன்.
context: When you avoid spam calls.
explain: "Never" shows something you do not do at all. "Pick up" means answer the phone.

en: Why didn't you answer my call?
context: When you are a little upset about a missed call.
explain: "Didn't" plus the base verb forms a negative question in the past.

en: Who was calling you just now?
context: When you see someone finish a call.
explain: "Was calling" shows an action that was in progress a moment ago.

en: My phone battery is almost dead.
context: When you must end the call soon.
explain: "Almost dead" is a spoken way to say there is very little battery.

alt.en: My phone is about to switch off.
alt.tamil: என் போன் இப்போ ஸ்விட்ச் ஆஃப் ஆகப் போகுது.

en: Please speak a little slowly.
context: When you cannot follow fast speech.
explain: "A little" softens the request. "Slowly" is an adverb for "speak".

en: Could you repeat that, please?
context: When you did not catch what was said.
explain: "Repeat that" is the simple way to ask someone to say it again.

en: I'll be in a meeting, so please text me.
tamil: நான் மீட்டிங்ல இருப்பேன், அதனால எனக்கு டெக்ஸ்ட் பண்ணுங்க.
context: When you cannot take calls.
explain: "So" joins a reason with a result. "Text me" means send a message.

en: Let's do a video call tonight.
context: When you suggest seeing a friend or family online.
explain: "Let's" plus a base verb is used to make a suggestion.

en: I forgot to charge my phone last night.
tamil: நேத்து ராத்திரி என் போனை சார்ஜ் பண்ண மறந்துட்டேன்.
context: When your phone is off and you explain why.
explain: "Forgot to" plus a base verb means you did not do something you should have.

en: Thanks for calling us, have a lovely day.
tamil: எங்களுக்கு கூப்பிட்டதுக்கு நன்றி, இனிய நாளா அமையட்டும்.
context: How an agent ends a call politely.
explain: This is a polite closing line. "Thank you for" is followed by an -ing word.

en: I'll ring off now, bye.
context: When you finish a call.
explain: "Ring off" means to end a call. It is common in Indian English.

en: Is this the right number for the help desk?
context: When you are not sure whom you called.
explain: Start with "is" to ask a yes or no question about a fact.
